I have been growing cotton on these 2 mu for more years than I can count. My mother grew cotton here too. I know this land — I know where it drains slow in a wet year and where the soil crusts hard if I water too early. I do not need a pamphlet to tell me what to do.

I will plant late April, around Grain Rain, just as I always have. Soil needs to be warm enough or the seeds rot. I buy improved seed from the village supply co-op — not the expensive hybrids the younger farmers talk about. Those cost more and I am not confident I can manage them right. My improved variety is reliable and I know how it behaves.

Before planting I rotary-till the field and work in base fertilizer — compound fertilizer plus some extra urea. My soil here is not rich, so I do not skimp on nitrogen. Then I top-dress once during boll-setting when the plants are heavy. I have been doing this long enough to feel when the plants need feeding.

I will irrigate five times from my well: at seeding to get good germination, during budding, during flowering, during early boll formation, and once more if August is dry. Cotton cannot go thirsty when bolls are forming — that is where you lose your yield.

Bollworm is my biggest worry every year. I will spray six times through the season, more if infestation is heavy. My eyes are still good enough to scout the field myself.

I expect around 230 jin of seed cotton per mu. Not the best in the county, but steady. Enough for my household and a little to sell.
